There are two kinds of code cell.

## 1. Runs in the reader's browser

Use `{pyodide}` for small demos (numpy, pandas). The reader can edit and re-run it.

```{pyodide}
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
p_missing = 0.3                      # try changing this
x = rng.normal(50, 10, size=1000)
observed = x[rng.random(1000) > p_missing]
print(f"true mean {x.mean():.2f}, observed mean {observed.mean():.2f}, n = {observed.size}")
```

## 2. Runs on your machine, results are stored

Use `{python}` or `{r}` for anything heavy (PyMC, brms). Render the post locally once;
the outputs are saved under `_freeze/` and committed, so the website build never re-fits the model.

```python
# shown here as plain code; change the fence to {python} to have Quarto run it
import pymc as pm
```
